Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

ISS4600.1968 

Indian Standard 

SPECinCATION FOR 
FLEXIBLE SHAFTS 

0. FOREWORD 

OJ This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 15 May 1968, after the draft finalized by the Transmission Devices 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering 
Division Oouncil. 

0.2 This standard has been prepared with a view to achieving uniformity 
in the manufacture and easy mterchangeability of parts of flexible shi^s. 

03 Flexible shafts make it possible to transmit power or to provide remote 
control between any two points with a single self-contained element, 
regardless of the relative position of the two points or obstacles on the path 
between them. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, emress- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960'*. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be 
the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



L SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements and principal dimensions of 
flexible shafts for industrial purposes. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2*0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 

2.1 bmer Shaft ~ The bare working element without end fittings. 

2Jt Shmlh End Ftednan — Parts for fastening to the ends of the inner shaft 
by means of which the flexible shaft assembly is connected to the driving 
and driven elements. 



*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rmsid )« 

3 



3L3 Immr Shaft AsMinbly— The inner shaft with end fittings attached^ 
or one with integrally formed squares. 

2A Ooter Caafaig — A flexible covering in the form of tube which acts as 
a runway or guide for the inner shaft, protects it from dirt and injury, 
assists in retaining lubrication and prevents formation of loops in operation. 

Z5 Outer Caaiag End Fittiiupi — Fftrts used for fastening to the ends of 
the outer casinff, oy means of which the outer casing is connected or 
coupled to the driving and driven elements {see Fig. 1 ). 

2.6 Outer Gftsisig Assembly — The outer casing with end fittings 
attached. 

2.7 PIsKflbls fluift Assembly — A combination of inner shaft assembly 
and co-ordinated outer casing assembly. Pkactically all applications of 
the flexible shaft require a flexible shaft assembly. 

2M Eflid StUTener — A member helically wound and slipped over either 
end of the outer casing to prevent excessive bend of the shaft near 
the ends. 

23 Lay of the Shaft— The pitch direction of the outer layer of shaft. 
Depending upon the direction of lay, shaft shall be specified as right lay or 
left lay. 

2.10 Directhm of Rotatioii— The direction which tightens up the outer 
layer of the inner shaft. 



S. MATERIALS AND MECHANICAL PROPERTIES 



S4 Immmr Shaft — The inner shaft shall be made of spring steel according 
toIS:727.1964^ 



SJt Ovter TVT%g — The outer casing shall have an inner liner of 
suitable steel having a minimum tensile strength of 120 kgf/nun* with rolled 
rounded edge. 

C DIMENSIONS 

44 The dimensions of flexible shaft assembly and their parts shall be as 
given in Table 1 (see Fig. 1 ).

5. DESIGNATION 

5.1 Flexible shaft assembly shall be designated by the commonly known 
name, a letter ' L ' or ^ R ' representing left lay or right lay of the outer layer 
of the inner shaft, by the diameter of the inner shaft, length of the 
inner shaft and the number of this standard. 

Example: 

A flexible shaft having left lay as the outer layer of the inner 
shaft with inner shaft diameter of 12 mm and length 2000 mm slutU 
be designated as: 

Flexible Shaft L. 12x2000 IS:4600 

6. TESTS 

6.1 Visiiml Inspection — The shaft shall be inspected for obvious flaws, 
kinks, bends, looseness, etc. 

6.2 Roll Test — A length of about 1 000 mm or more is taken, and is laid 
on the floor in a slight curve of about 10 metres diameter and rolled back- 
and forth at the centre by foot The shaft shall roll smoothly throughout 
its length without offering resistance and without jerking or flapping abotit. 
The extreme ends may flap a little. 

6 J Locking Diameter Test— The flexible shaft assembly is looped and 
the junction is held in* hand. One end of the flexible shaft is pulled so as 
to reduce the diameter of the loop until the shaft assembly is felt to oflfer 
considerable resistance. The diameter of the loop is then measured. It 
shall be within 20 times the diameter of the inner shaft. The loop shall be 
as nearly circular as possible and there shall not be any obvious difference 
in the radius of curvature at two adjacent points. 

7. MARKING 

7.1 All shafts shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade-mark 
with designation of the shafts. 

7.1.1 Flexible shafts may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 



Marie ii governed kjy the provisions of the 
^farks) Act and the Rules and Ranilations 
foducts covered by an Indian Standard 



NoT9 — Tlie use of the ISI Certification 
Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks ] 
made thereunder* The ISI Mark on products 

conveys the anurance that they have been produced to cooqply with the rec|uirenenti 
of that standard under a welMefined system of inspection^ tpong and quahty control 
which is devised and superviied by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI maiked 
products are also continuously checked by ISI for contormity to that standard as a 
ftircher safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained 
from the Indian Standards Institution.

4. DIMENSIONS 

4.1 The dimensions of flexible shall assembly covered in this standard are 
of two types, namely, Type A and Type B as given below. 

4.1.1 Type A — Threaded shaft end fittings on both ends with the outer 
casing sliding at the driving end. The dimensions of Type A flexible shaft 
assembly and their parts shall be as given in Table 1 . 

4.1.2 Type B — F.ixed outer casing end fittings on both ends and sliding 
shaft end nttings at the driven end. The dimensions of Type B flexible 
shaft assembly and their parts shall be as given in Table 2** 



Grl
